subsystems.name: Display and optics
subsystems.role: presents a separate high-resolution image to each eye.

subsystems.name: Tracking and sensing
subsystems.role: determines the headset's position and the user's hands in real time.

subsystems.name: Pass-through and compositing
subsystems.role: captures the real world and blends it with rendered content.

subsystems.name: Compute and power
subsystems.role: runs rendering, tracking and applications on the headset.

subsystems.name: Audio and input
subsystems.role: lets the user hear and interact.

subsystems.name: Structure and ergonomics
subsystems.role: distributes weight and holds optics in place.

buildSteps.title: Design the optical stack
buildSteps.detail: Simulate field of view, resolution and distortion; choose between pancake lenses (folded optics for slimness) or waveguides (for see-through MR).

buildSteps.title: Fabricate microdisplays
buildSteps.detail: Micro-OLED panels are built on silicon backplanes with organic layers; LCDs use thin-film transistors on glass. Pixel density can exceed 3000 pixels per inch.

buildSteps.title: Make the lenses
buildSteps.detail: Pancake lenses use partially reflective surfaces and polarized light to fold the light path; waveguides use diffractive gratings to guide light to the eye.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the sensor suite
buildSteps.detail: Cameras, inertial measurement unit, depth sensors and eye-tracking cameras are positioned and connected to the main board.

buildSteps.title: Build the compute board
buildSteps.detail: A system-on-chip, memory, storage, battery and cooling are integrated into a compact module.

buildSteps.title: Write the software stack
buildSteps.detail: SLAM algorithms fuse camera and inertial data to track the headset; hand tracking, rendering, and a low-latency compositor run on the chip.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate each unit
buildSteps.detail: Camera intrinsics, lens distortion and display alignment are measured and corrected so virtual objects stay anchored to the real world.

buildSteps.title: Final assembly and test
buildSteps.detail: The headset is assembled, fitted with straps and cushions, and tested for comfort, image quality and tracking accuracy.

prerequisites.why: dense screens near the eye are needed to avoid visible pixels.
cameras and inertial sensors must locate the headset without external base stations.
they make headsets slim enough to wear while preserving image quality.
tracking the gaze allows rendering only where the eye looks, saving power, but is not yet universal.
untethered high-resolution MR needs either fast wireless links or batteries that are light enough.

pathway.milestone: standalone headsets with color pass-through, hand tracking and inside-out tracking
pathway.unlocks: spatial computing for work, design and entertainment without external base stations.

pathway.milestone: higher resolution, wider field of view, and eye tracking as standard
pathway.unlocks: text and detail sharp enough for everyday productivity.

pathway.milestone: glasses-like form factor using waveguides and microLED displays
pathway.unlocks: all-day wear and true augmented reality.

pathway.milestone: persistent shared virtual spaces anchored to the real world
pathway.unlocks: seamless blending of physical and digital life.
